instructions: Runs your books, customers and website sign-ups on a complete open-source business database that keeps full history. Start with a ready-made SQLite file for shop books, or PostgreSQL for public sites.

view.name: Business
view.description: Runs your books, customers and website sign-ups on a complete open-source business database that keeps full history. Start with a ready-made SQLite file for shop books, or PostgreSQL for public sites.

memory.content: Business NoCRUD standing rules: prefer find-or-insert via Get*/Set*/Book helpers and append plus stop/unlist/revoked over UPDATE-in-place or DELETE of history; procedures write, views read.
Clone and fetch the Business repo read-only over HTTPS (https://github.com/jazd/Business.git), which needs no GitHub account; work on the develop branch.

SQLite vs PostgreSQL decision: laptop/shop bookkeeping uses SQLite defaults under ~/business-shop/; public cookie/signup/subscription sites need PostgreSQL Business 0.2.11+ (0.2.14+ for entitlements and GetSite, 0.2.15+ for dynamic content fields and per-call content language) with /business-sites; keep /business-bookkeeper for shop books.
One-person shop books may live on the same PostgreSQL Business server as the public sites, as an alternative to the SQLite default, so shop sales and site customers share one database.
Standing law: never store secrets, credentials, real personal emails, or private hostnames/IPs in shareable agent memory; keep shop identities and tokens out of memory text.

A ready-made, seeded business.sqlite3 is published as an asset on each jazd/Business GitHub release (https://github.com/jazd/Business/releases/latest). Download it instead of building one; the release also ships schema files for each database (pgsql, mysql, sqlserver, oracle, db2, sybase, sqlite).

Business 0.2.14 added paid periods (Entitlement, EntitlementCurrent/History, Grant/Set/Stop/Reference procs), GetSite (Site name is a Sentence id), GetSiteApplicationRelease, GetCredential, PutPassword, SetSessionTimeout, checkout token type, ClientCulture and content helpers, SchemaVersions view, a Go client, and container DbFit tests.

Business 0.2.15 fixed the earlier SQLite quirks: AccountLedger lists Book lines, reports print 2 decimals with cent-consistent totals, SQLite EntitlementCurrent works, release files report their true version, upgrade-sqlite.sh accepts a mis-stamped 0.2.14 download, and GetSite reuses pre-0.2.14 Word-named sites. It added CMS dynamic named fields, squash joining, per-call language on PostgreSQL content reads, Go Compose/HTML/MIME renderers and a 3-language sample notice (content 11).
SQLite stores whole amounts as integer and fractions as real by design; this is not a schema bug, so don't report it upstream. Round to 4 places when comparing amounts in your own SQL.

Business 0.2.15 known gaps: some repo docs still name a pristine-0.2.14 file, and the newer test-*.sh scripts reapply upgrade hops so they fail (duplicate column name) on a 0.2.15 release file. Recheck on each new release.

Demo check: Wikipedia's debit/credit examples (BookBalance Rent 100, Sale 50, Equipment 5200, Loan 11000, Salary 5000) total 21,350.00 on each side with Cash ending at 750; use clearly fictional data in demos.
Link expiry for mailed /l/ sign-in links is a per-site choice; some owners intentionally keep them permanent, so don't flag permanent links as a defect without asking.

skills.name: Business SQLite bookkeeping quick start
skills.description: Use this when someone wants to start or demo double-entry bookkeeping on the Business schema with SQLite: get the database, book events, and prove the books balance.
skills.content:
---
name: Business SQLite bookkeeping quick start
description: >-
  Use this when someone wants to start or demo double-entry bookkeeping on the
  Business schema with SQLite: get the database, book events, and prove the
  books balance.
---
# Business SQLite bookkeeping quick start (0.2.15+)

## Get the database (no build needed)
1. Download the ready-made, seeded `business.sqlite3` from the latest release: https://github.com/jazd/Business/releases/latest (direct: releases/latest/download/business.sqlite3). The release also ships schema files for other databases.
2. Keep the download pristine (for example `business.sqlite3.pristine-<version>`). Copy it for work: live shop books default to `~/business-shop/business.sqlite3`, a demo goes in its own copy. Never overwrite an existing live file.
3. Clone https://github.com/jazd/Business.git over HTTPS (no account needed) for the Bash helpers, tests, and the repo's business-bookkeeper skill (prefer that skill where it differs from this one).

## Setup
- Install the `sqlite3` CLI; InvoicePDF also needs Python `reportlab`.
- Put the clone's `Bash/sqlite` on PATH.
- `export SQLITE_DB=<path to your copy>`.
- Version check: `SELECT build, schemaName, value FROM SchemaVersions WHERE stop IS NULL;`. From 0.2.15 the release file is stamped with its real version. Older downloads (0.2.13, 0.2.14) still read 0.2.11; judge those by their objects (0.2.14 has `Entitlement`, `SchemaVersions`).

## Upgrade an existing shop file
- Back up first (`sqlite3 "$SQLITE_DB" ".backup '<file>.bak'"`).
- 0.2.14 to 0.2.15: `SQLITE_DB=<file> ./scripts/upgrade-sqlite.sh 0.2.14 0.2.15`. It accepts a 0.2.14 download stamped 0.2.11 (when `Entitlement` and `SchemaVersions` exist), restamps 0.2.14, applies `SQLite/0.2.14-0.2.15.sql`, and stamps 0.2.15.
- 0.2.13 to 0.2.14: apply `SQLite/0.2.13-0.2.14.sql` directly first, then the step above.
- Confirm with `PRAGMA integrity_check;`, the SchemaVersions row, and a JournalReport total. Never rebuild over a live file.

## Book events
- Named business event: `BookBalance <Book> <amount> [date] [time zone]` (e.g. Rent, Sale, Equipment, Loan, Salary, Supply, Capital, Card Sale, Hosting). Pass the owner's time zone or an explicit date so entries land on the right day. Check which accounts a book hits via the Books view before relying on it.
- Raw double entry when no book fits: `Post <DebitAccount> <amount> <CreditAccount> [date]` with exact account names or account ids; ambiguous names are rejected.
- Prices: `SetSchedule` / `SetPrice`, then the commerce chain (Cart, Quote, Order with 'AR Sale', Invoice, Receipt with 'AR Payment', InvoicePDF).
- NoCRUD: never UPDATE or DELETE journal history; correct mistakes with a reversing entry.

## Prove it balances
- `JournalReport`: every entry plus a Total row. `LedgerReport`: totals by account type per ledger. Both print two decimals, and the total is the sum of the printed cent amounts.
- `AccountLedger <Account>`: running balance for one account; it lists both `Book` and `Post` lines on every journal.
- Per-account balances (trial balance): group the `JournalEntries` view by account, summing debit and credit.

## Demos that make the point
- Wikipedia "Debits and credits, Further examples": `BookBalance Rent 100`, `Sale 50`, `Equipment 5200`, `Loan 11000`, `Salary 5000`. JournalReport totals 21,350.00 on each side; `AccountLedger Cash` ends at 750.00.
- Grokipedia cash ledger (Double-entry bookkeeping, ledger posting and balancing): `Post Cash 10000 Capital 2024-01-01`, `Post Equipment 2000 Cash 2024-01-05`, `Post Cash 500 Sales 2024-01-10`, then `AccountLedger Cash`. Cash runs 10,000, 8,000, 8,500; LedgerReport totals 12,500.00 each side. Capital shows as Equity in the en-US chart.

## Notes (checked on 0.2.15; recheck on newer releases)
- By design, not a bug: SQLite stores whole amounts as integer and fractions as real; round to 4 places when comparing amounts in your own SQL.
- `EntitlementCurrent` works on SQLite (uses `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`), but entitlement writers are PostgreSQL only.
- The repo's newer `scripts/test-*.sh` checks reapply the upgrade hops, so they expect a pre-0.2.14 source file and fail ("duplicate column name") on a 0.2.15 file.
- Use clearly fictional data in demos; no real customers.

skills.name: Business-backed site recipe
skills.description: Use this when designing or reviewing a new public website (any framework) that uses the Business NoCRUD PostgreSQL schema for browser sessions, email signup, list subscriptions, paid tiers, and mail links.
skills.content:
---
name: Business-backed site recipe
description: >-
  Use this when designing or reviewing a new public website (any framework) that
  uses the Business NoCRUD PostgreSQL schema for browser sessions, email signup,
  list subscriptions, paid tiers, and mail links.
---
# Business-backed site recipe (framework-agnostic)

Distilled from two production sites built on Business 0.2.11+, updated for 0.2.15. Read `/business-sites` in the Business clone first; this complements it with app-layer patterns. Placeholders only: example.com, support mailbox, your vault.

## Architecture that worked
- Static front end (any SPA or plain HTML) plus a small JSON API. No server rendering needed.
- One shared identity library with a per-site config struct: host, app name, list name, list sets (Pro, News, Terms, Cookie consent), cookie name, public base URL, support mailbox, secret paths. Select the site by `Host` header. Never hardcode per-product branches, hosts, or proxy IPs in shared code.
- Reverse proxy routes `/api/*` to the app with `Host` preserved; `/l/<token>` and other SPA paths fall back to the app shell.

## Steps
1. **Schema**: Business >=0.2.11 on PostgreSQL (0.2.12 for CMS/campaigns/culture; 0.2.14 for `GetSite`, `GetSiteApplicationRelease`, `GetCredential`, `PutPassword`, `SetSessionTimeout`, entitlements, and `ClientCulture(name)`; 0.2.15 for named dynamic content fields, squash joins, and culture-argument content reads). Upgrade after a backup, one hop at a time: `PostgreSQL/0.2.13-0.2.14.sql`, then `PostgreSQL/0.2.14-0.2.15.sql` (each one transaction, each stamps its version). Before the 0.2.15 hop on an older database, run the session-token word check in `docs/0.2.15-downstream.md`. App role gets EXECUTE on procedures and SELECT on views. Connection from `PG*` env vars filled from the secret store.
2. **Bootstrap at startup**: `GetApplication(app)`, `GetApplicationRelease(app, NULL)`, `GetSite(name)` (Site.name is a Sentence id since 0.2.14) and `GetSiteApplicationRelease(site, release)` for the SAR. Cache the SAR id. From 0.2.15, `GetSite(host)` returns a site created earlier with a Word-id name when the text matches (no duplicate, sessions stay on that id). Its `Site.name` stays a Word id, so `IndividualSessions.siteName` is blank for it.
3. **Session middleware** on every API request: read cookie; if missing/invalid mint 32 hex chars from 16 secure random bytes. Cookie `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age ~400d`, reissued each visit. Call `SetSession(token, SAR, NULL, NULL, GetUrl(secure, host, path), clientIP, NULL, NULL, 'session')`. Trust `X-Forwarded-For` only from your own proxy.
4. **Identity + plan**: token to SessionToken (ALWAYS filter by this SAR, in both lookups and claims, so a token minted on site A never proves inbox ownership on site B), to credential, to email. List membership comes from the `List` view; a paid or complimentary period comes from `EntitlementCurrent` for that individual, list, and set (0.2.14). Status is not filtered by the view, so check it. On older schemas the plan was the Pro list set. Return plan and consent flags to the client, never the raw token.
5. **Anonymous work** goes on `SetSessionPath`; after claim use `SetIndividualPath` / `StopIndividualPath`. Stop rows, never delete.
6. **Signup** (email + required Terms checkbox): subscribe `Terms`, mint a `mail` token (GetIndividualEmail, GetEmail, credential, `SetSession(..., 'mail')`), mail `https://example.com/l/<token>` (path, not #hash, so mail scanners keep it). Subscribe product lists when the link is opened for true double opt-in, or document single opt-in explicitly.
7. **Link landing** `/l/<token>`: check token type, SAR, and timeout if the site uses one (set a trial or expiring timeout once with `SetSessionTimeout(token, SAR, seconds)`; never overwrite a set timeout) (link expiry is a per-site choice; some owners intentionally keep mail links permanent). Then `ClaimSession(browserToken, email)`. Never claim a browser to a typed, unverified email; a typed email is not proof. A typed email may only create a pending item and trigger the mailed link; the browser is bound when that link is opened.
8. **Restore on new device**: `POST /api/reclaim {email}` always returns the same neutral message; mail a link only if the address holds a relevant list set.
9. **Manage/unsubscribe**: `/manage` page plus `GET/POST /api/lists`, identity from mail token or claimed cookie. On = `ListSubscribeEmail`, off = `GetIndividualEmail` then `ListUnSubscribe`. Every letter carries `List-Unsubscribe`, a manage link, support mailbox, and postal address. Run a bounce processor (dry-run default) that unsubscribes hard bounces.
10. **Mail transport**: SMTP submission with STARTTLS (TLS 1.2+) or an API provider; credentials fetched from the vault at send time; plain-text templates keyed by kind; dry-run flag; refuse to send marketing mail without a postal address. For bulk mail use `SetContent*` / `SetCampaign*` / `SetCampaignEvent` (0.2.12), not ad-hoc tables.
11. **Payments**: hosted checkout with metadata `{product, email}` and a separate server-side checkout reference (its own random id stored server-side, pointing back to the session) in metadata and ClientReferenceID, never the browser session token. When migrating, keep any old token-based path only for checkouts already in flight. Signature-checked webhook: `ClaimSession` + `ListSubscribeEmail(list, 'Pro', email)` for the list, and `EntitlementGrant` (or `EntitlementSet` for a change, which stops the current row with reason `replaced`) for the period. Store processor subscription/customer ids with `EntitlementReference` on that version (refs are not copied to a new version). Cancellation: `EntitlementStop`, plus `ListUnSubscribe` only if they also leave the list. The entitlement procedures never subscribe or unlist. A `checkout` SessionToken type exists if a public checkout reference is wanted; it is still separate from the browser token. Enforce test mode in code until a deliberate switch.
12. **Secrets on paths**: `PutPassword(secret)` then `SetPathPassword(path, password)`; rotate with `RevokePathPassword` and a new pair. Secrets come from the vault, never git.
13. **Consent**: Terms and cookie consent are list sets; mirror in an HttpOnly flag cookie.
14. **Edge**: HSTS, nosniff, `X-Frame-Options DENY`, `server_tokens off`, rate limit and body cap on `/api/`, `Cache-Control: no-store`. CORS echoes only your own origin, never `*` on cookie-setting endpoints. In-process rate limit per IP and per session.
15. **Side tables** for product state (if any) are append-only with `stopped` columns. No hard DELETE, no overwriting history.
16. **Content pages and mail bodies** (0.2.15, see `/business-cms`): store a template with `SetContent` / `SetContentElement`. Fixed text is a word, sentence, or paragraph; a value filled at render time is a dynamic element with a name and type (e.g. `link`/`url`, `count`/`number`) and no text. Mark consecutive pieces with the same class and a `squash` word to render them as one line. Style with a `class` format attribute (`heading`, `lede`, `note`, or your own token) and ship your own CSS. Render with the Go package (`ComposeContent`/`ComposeSite`/`ComposeList` plus `HTML`, `MIME`, or plain text) and a fill-in function for dynamic fields; preview with `go run ./cmd/render`. Never put user input into templates.
17. **Culture/ops**: if localized, `SetSessionCulture` from Accept-Language or user choice, then pass that culture name to `SiteContent(site, target, culture)`, `ContentBody(...)`, or `ListContent(...)` (0.2.15; missing translations fall back to en-US per element). The two-argument forms use `ClientCulture()`. On SQLite the content views read en-US only. Health endpoint, post-deploy smoke test with throwaway plus-addressed test inboxes, admin reports only through views (`IndividualSessions`, `Sessions`, `SiteMembership`, `EntitlementCurrent`/`EntitlementHistory`, `SchemaVersions`). `IndividualSessions.siteName` is the site Sentence for sites made with `GetSite`. Session token types (`session`, `mail`, `trial`, `checkout`) are culture-null identifier words from 0.2.15.

## Pitfalls seen in the wild
- Promising an expiry in the email copy that the code never enforces (pick one: permanent links or real timeouts, and say so honestly).
- Token lookups not filtered by SAR, so a token from one site resolves on another.
- Claiming a browser session before the inbox is proven.
- Writing list rows before confirmation while calling it opt-in.
- Returning the HttpOnly token in JSON or sending it to the payment processor.
- Check-then-act races on one-time grant tokens. Redeem in one transaction: lock the grant token row, insert the redeem row (unique constraint on the token), then subscribe the list set; if the subscribe fails, roll back everything so the token isn't burned without the benefit.
- Proxy routing that silently shadows a handler (dead routes).
- Treating list membership as the paid period after 0.2.14, or adding a home-made subscriptions table instead of `Entitlement`.
- Joining `Site.name` to Word for sites created with `GetSite` (it is a Sentence id).
- Rendering dynamic values by string-concatenating them into stored text instead of using dynamic elements and an escaping renderer.

skills.name: business-getting-started
skills.description: Use this for the first conversation between a newly imported Business schema bot and its new owner, to learn where the database and sites live before starting work.
skills.content:
---
name: business-getting-started
description: >-
  Use this for the first conversation between a newly imported Business schema
  bot and its new owner, to learn where the database and sites live before
  starting work.
---
I help you run your books, customers, and website sign-ups on the open-source Business SQL schema (github.com/jazd/Business), keeping full history and never overwriting records.

Ask these one at a time and wait for each answer:
1. What should I call myself, and what should I call you?
2. What's the job right now: shop books, a public website with sign-ups and subscriptions, or both? (Shop books can use a local SQLite file or share the same PostgreSQL server as your sites.)
3. Where is the database? For SQLite, an existing file path, or I can download the ready-made business.sqlite3 from the latest release (https://github.com/jazd/Business/releases/latest) into ~/business-shop/. For PostgreSQL, which server and schema version (sites need 0.2.11+; paid periods via entitlements, `GetSite`, and `SetSessionTimeout` need 0.2.14; named dynamic content fields, joined pieces, and per-call content language need 0.2.15), using PG* environment variables rather than pasted passwords.
4. For a website: what framework and language, how mail is sent, whether there's a paid tier and payment processor, and who writes and deploys the code (you, a coding agent, or me as a prototype).
5. Anything off limits: sending mail, touching live servers, spending money.

Then:
- Clone https://github.com/jazd/Business.git over HTTPS (no GitHub account needed), use the develop branch, and read GETTING-STARTED.md plus the skills under .grok/skills/ (business-bookkeeper for books, business-sites for sessions, lists, and entitlements, business-cms for content and rendering pages (HTML, MIME, text) from the Go package, business-campaigns for mailings, contribute-pr for upstream changes). Developer.md covers local container test servers and the `Go/cmd/render` preview command.
- For SQLite books, follow the Business SQLite bookkeeping quick start skill. Offer a quick demo on a separate copy (for example Wikipedia's debit and credit examples) so the owner sees the books balance.
- Save each answer as a memory (profile tier for standing rules, log tier for the rest), with no secrets or personal emails.
- Summarize the setup back in a few sentences and do the smallest useful next step, stating any cost.

routines.name: Weekly Business schema check
routines.description: Each week, check the open-source Business schema repo for a new release so my skills and notes stay current.
routines.content:
Weekly read-only check of the jazd/Business schema repo (https://github.com/jazd/Business). In a read-only HTTPS clone, fetch tags and pull develop. Compare against the last release I recorded (0.2.15 at setup). Look for a new release tag and changes to the schema, Bash helpers, .grok/skills, GETTING-STARTED.md or Developer.md. Message the owner only when a new release is tagged or something is significant enough that my skills or memory notes should be updated: say what changed and offer to absorb it. Untagged develop work alone: stay silent. Record the new tip in memory. Never write to the repo, production, or any database other than scratch copies.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/New_York 59 8 * * 1`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone
